([[Saint Paul, Minnesota]]) | college = *[[Indian Hills Community College|Indian Hills CC]] (2020–2021) *[[Buffalo Bulls men's basketball|Buffalo]] (2021–2023) *[[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]] (2023–2025) | draft_year = 2025 | career_start = 2025 | years1 = {{nbay|2025|full=y}} | team1 = [[Denver Nuggets]] | years2 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025–2026]] | team2 = →[[Grand Rapids Gold]] | highlights = * [[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] Sixth Man Award (2025) * First-team [[List of All-Big 12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big 12]] (2025) * Third-team All-[[Mid-American Conference|MAC]] ([[2022–23 Mid-American Conference men's basketball season|2023]]) }} '''Curtis Jalen Jones''' (born October 4, 2001) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Denver Nuggets]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), on a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Grand Rapids Gold]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played college basketball for the [[Indian Hills Warriors]], [[Buffalo Bulls men's basketball|Buffalo Bulls]] and [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State Cyclones]]. ==Early life and high school career== Jones grew up in [[Minneapolis, Minnesota]] and initially attended [[South High School (Minnesota)|South High School]] before transferring to [[Cretin-Derham Hall High School]].{{cite web|url=https://spokesman-recorder.com/2024/05/22/curtis-jones-prep-college-career/|title=Curtis Jones' journey: A high school and college basketball career|work=[[Minnesota Spokesman-Recorder]]|date=May 22, 2024|access-date=February 13, 2025}} Jones had no Division I or Division II scholarship offers out of high school.{{cite web|url=https://www.startribune.com/curtis-jones-iowa-state-buffalo-cretin-derham-hall-juco/601208709|title=Cretin-Derham Hall grad Curtis Jones takes different path to stardom for Iowa State|first=Marcus|last=Fuller|work=[[Minnesota Star Tribune]]|date=January 21, 2025|access-date=February 12, 2025}} ==College career== Jones began his college career at [[Indian Hills Community College]].{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/inside-iowa-state-star-curtis-jones-rise-from-junior-college-afterthought-to-potential-all-american/|title=Inside Iowa State star Curtis Jones' rise from junior college afterthought to potential All-American|first=Isaac|last=Trotter|website=[[CBS Sports]]|date=January 16, 2025|access-date=February 12, 2025}} He averaged 12.1 points, 6.0 rebounds, and 5.5 assists per game as a freshman with the Warriors.{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/iowa-state/article/curtis-jones-continuing-development-as-shooting-threat-for-isu-basketball-2023-214030693/|title=Curtis Jones continuing development as shooting threat for ISU|first=Payne|last=Blazevich|website=[[247Sports.com]]|date=August 9, 2023|access-date=February 12, 2025}} After the season, Jones transferred to [[Buffalo Bulls men's basketball|Buffalo]]. He averaged 2.5 points and 1.3 assists in 28 games, all off the bench, in his first season with the Bulls.{{cite web|url=https://www.wivb.com/jerry-sullivan/sullivan-throwback-style-helps-ubs-curtis-jones-make-most-of-unexpected-opportunity/|title=Sullivan: 'Throwback' style helps UB's Curtis Jones make most of unexpected opportunity|first=Jerry|last=Sullivan|website=[[WIVB-TV|WIVB.com]]|date=December 9, 2022|access-date=February 12, 2025}} Jones was named third-team All-MAC as a junior after averaging 15.0 points, 4.8 rebounds, and 3.0 assists per game.{{cite web|url=https://buffalonews.com/sports/college/ub-guard-curtis-jones-named-to-all-mac-mens-basketball-third-team/article_45770c0a-bdf3-11ed-960d-e34402e979e1.html|title=UB guard Curtis Jones named to All-MAC men's basketball third team|work=[[The Buffalo News]]|date=March 8, 2023|access-date=February 13, 2025}} After the season, he entered the NCAA transfer portal.{{cite web|url=https://buffalonews.com/sports/college/ub-mens-basketball-guard-curtis-jones-enters-transfer-portal/article_839fc98e-c7f0-11ed-8b89-fb2406bedd73.html|title=UB men's basketball guard Curtis Jones enters transfer portal|work=[[The Buffalo News]]|date=March 21, 2023|access-date=February 13, 2025}} Jones transferred to [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]].{{cite web|url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/college/iowa-state/cyclone-insider/2023/04/17/iowa-state-basketball-curtis-jones-transfer-portal-commitment-2023-24-roster/70123728007/|title=Iowa State men's basketball picks up former Buffalo guard Curtis Jones in the transfer portal|first=Alyssa|last=Hertel|work=[[The Des Moines Register]]|date=April 17, 2023|access-date=February 12, 2025}} He averaged 11.0 points, 2.9 rebounds and 2.0 assists per game in his first season with the Cyclones.{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/nba/draft/newsfeed/nba-draft-iowa-state-curtis-jones-strengthening-big-12-player-of-the-year-case|title=Iowa State's Curtis Jones strengthening Big 12 Player of the Year case|first=Matt|last=Coletti|website=[[SI.com]]|date=January 27, 2025|access-date=February 13, 2025}} == Professional career == On June 27, 2025, Jones signed an [[Exhibit 10]] contract with the [[Denver Nuggets]] after going unselected in the [[2025 NBA draft]].{{Cite web |date=2025-06-27 |title=Curtis Jones Signs with Denver Nuggets |url=https://cyclones.com/news/2025/6/27/mens-basketball-curtis-jones-signs-with-denver-nuggets |access-date=2025-07-17 |website=Iowa State University Athletics |language=}} On July 20, after a standout summer league showing, Jones signed a two-way contract with the Nuggets.{{Cite web |last=Schubert |first=Matt |date=20 July 2025 |title=Nuggets, guard Curtis Jones agree to two-way contract, source says |url=https://www.denverpost.com/2025/07/20/curtis-jones-nuggets-two-way-contract/ |access-date=23 July 2025 |website=denverpost.com}} In July 2026, Jones joined the [[Boston Celtics]] for
